findings.question: q-chemistry-matter-0018
findings.quote:
- text: 'Only crystals have a definite volume.'
        rationale: |
          This equates definite volume with crystalline order. Both are solid properties in familiar examples. Check whether an amorphous solid can retain volume.
      - text: 'Amorphous solids always fill any vessel like gases.'
        rationale: |
          This confuses lack of a repeating lattice with the gas state. Disorder may sound like gas motion. Check whether the material is still solid.
      - text: 'Every solid has exactly the same repeating lattice.'
findings.problem: All three distractors use conspicuous absolute wording (Only, always, or Every ... exactly the same), while the keyed statement does not. This pattern lets a test-wise student select the sole restrained statement without knowing how crystalline and amorphous solids differ.
findings.fix: Use plausible distractors with parallel, neutral wording about particle arrangement, without concentrating absolute qualifiers in the wrong choices.

findings.question: q-chemistry-matter-0019
findings.quote: Its charged particles can show collective behavior.
findings.problem: Collective behavior is an unexplained technical phrase. A Grade 5 reader is not told what the particles do, and this extra sentence does not help explain the defining feature asked for.
findings.fix: Delete this sentence, or replace it with a simple explanation that plasma contains charged particles because some atoms have lost or gained electrons.
